c.tagline: A rebuilding mountain town in Canada's largest Rocky Mountain national park, still as wild and welcoming as ever

card: Contactless and card payment are the norm virtually everywhere; cash is rarely needed.

taxi.color: no standard livery — mostly private sedans and vans
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard; book ahead in peak summer season given limited fleet size

emergency.note: Parks Canada visitor safety staff and mountain rescue respond to backcountry incidents

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Jasper's small townsite is fully walkable, with Patricia Street shops and restaurants close together; Maligne Lake, Athabasca Falls, and the Columbia Icefield require a car or organized tour along the Icefields Parkway.

safety.safety: Very safe; Jasper is a well-managed national park town with low crime, though the community and infrastructure are still actively rebuilding after the July 2024 wildfire that destroyed roughly a third of the townsite's buildings
safety.crime: Petty theft is rare; the main practical concerns for 2026 visitors are checking current road/trail closures and campground availability given ongoing restoration work, and standard wildlife safety on trails

hood_landmark.Jasper Townsite / Patricia Street: Jasper SkyTram base station and downtown shops
hood_landmark.Pyramid Lake / Patricia Lake: Pyramid Lake with Pyramid Mountain views
hood_landmark.Old Fort Point: Old Fort Point trail and Athabasca River viewpoint
hood_landmark.Icefields Parkway Gateway: Athabasca Falls and the route toward the Columbia Icefield

avoid.reason: No crime hotspots, but keep a safe distance from elk and bears that wander into town, especially during autumn rut and spring calving.

hood_desc: The compact town center, currently mid-rebuild after the 2024 wildfire but with the majority of businesses, restaurants, and hotels reopened and welcoming visitors.
A scenic valley about 45 minutes from town, home to Maligne Lake's famous boat cruise to Spirit Island — one of the Rockies' most photographed spots.
A quiet lakeside area a short drive north of downtown, popular for canoeing and mountain reflections without the crowds of Lake Louise.
A riverside trail and viewpoint just outside downtown, offering an easy walk with sweeping views over the Athabasca River valley.
The southern entry point to the Icefields Parkway, with Athabasca Falls and the road continuing toward the Columbia Icefield and Banff.

water.note: Tap water is safe and excellent, sourced from the Rockies.

transit.sys: Seasonal local shuttle within the townsite; no year-round municipal transit
transit.pay: Cash or card depending on operator
transit.map: Check jasper.travel for current seasonal shuttle routes
transit.note: A car or organized tour is the practical way to reach Maligne Lake, the Columbia Icefield, and other sights outside the townsite; check Parks Canada's dashboard for current trail and campground closures tied to wildfire recovery

transport.air: Nearest major airport is Edmonton International (YEG), about 360 km / 4.5 hours away; Calgary (YYC) is a further alternative via the Icefields Parkway (~4 hrs)
transport.train: VIA Rail's Canadian train stops in Jasper on its transcontinental Toronto-Vancouver route, a scenic but infrequent option
transport.bus: Sundog Tours and Brewster Express coaches connect Jasper to Edmonton, Calgary, and Banff
transport.ferry: None — Jasper is inland in the Rocky Mountains with no ferry service
transport.car: Reachable via Highway 16 from Edmonton or the Icefields Parkway from Banff/Calgary; Highway 16 and all access routes are fully operational as of 2026 following the 2024 wildfire

airport.name: Edmonton International Airport
airport.transport: Sundog Tours shuttle bus or rental car; the drive along Highway 16 passes through scenic mountain foothills

net.m: Good 4G coverage in Jasper townsite; signal drops significantly in the backcountry and along remote stretches of the Icefields Parkway
net.w: Free wifi standard in reopened hotels and cafes
net.fwn: Free wifi available in hotels and cafes that have reopened post-wildfire
net.ap: A Canadian prepaid SIM or eSIM (Rogers, Telus, Bell) is easy to buy at Edmonton or Calgary Airport

tip.s: 15-18% is standard for hotel staff and tour guides
tip.r: 15-20% is customary at restaurants; often pre-suggested on the payment terminal
